newsitem.title: USA: California pub to give up Bank of Ireland name.
newsitem.headline: California pub to give up Bank of Ireland name.

text.p: A San Francisco bar and restaurant that offended a 200-year-old Irish bank by calling itself "The Bank of Ireland" has agreed to change its name, the bar's attorney said on Tuesday.

The pub said it would change its name to "The Irish Bank" by March 1. The bar's owners said they decided to give up the name because of the prohibitive costs of fighting the case in court. The bar has already taken its name off the Internet.
"My clients have acquiesced because they can't afford to do battle," said Terence Redmond, attorney for the restaurant. "The bank has what it wants."
Despite the name change, Redmond said the pub's legal dispute with the Dublin-based Bank of Ireland could continue because the bank wants the name withdrawn immediately.
Attorneys in New York representing the Bank of Ireland were not immediately available to comment.
The Bank of Ireland in late November sued the owners of the one-year-old bar in U.S. District Court in San Francisco, accusing the pub of misappropriating its name.
The bank said in papers filed in court that it had used the name "Bank of Ireland" since 1783 and the bar's use of the name "taints the bank's reputation."
"The bank does not wish to be affiliated in any way with the sale of alcohol under its name, or with the sale of food (such as the "Bank of Ireland Burger")," the lawsuit said.
The bar's co-owner Chris Martin opened the bar and restaurant with fellow Dubliner Rory Connolly last January.

They chose the name because it was in the heart of San Francisco's financial district and because they wanted to distinguish it from the city's many other Irish bars. They later created an Internet site, advertising the restaurant.
